text:
Maya: Noticing a weird UI quirk on the latency page: for /v1/embeddings in us-east, p95 (130ms) is lower than p50 (210ms) for the 30m window. Looks like the chart merged endpoints?
Jordan: Hmm. Do we have any recent routing changes or sampling config flips?
Maya: We rolled a routing tweak 45m ago to direct cold-starts to a warm-pool. Telemetry dump attached shows two sample groups: "warm-pool" (very low latencies, lots of sampled events) and "primary" (higher latencies but fewer raw samples).
Ravi: Classic: our rollup pipeline merges t-digests by raw observed count, but the sampler amplifies warm-pool events so raw_count != logical_traffic. When you naively merge, the global tdigest gets skewed toward warm-pool and the computed percentile order can invert.
Claire: Could bucketization also be involved? If we do coarse histogram rollups for long windows, interpolation can misorder percentiles, especially when one origin has spikey distribution.
Jordan: Good point. We should differentiate two failure modes in the runbook: 1) sample-weight bias (sampler imbalance) 2) rollup bucket interpolation artifact. Each has a distinct remediation.
Maya: Quick repro query I ran: ```SELECT sample_origin, count(*) AS raw_count, approx_percentile(response_ms,0.95) p95_approx, approx_percentile(response_ms,0.5) p50_approx FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/embeddings' AND ts > now()-30m GROUP BY sample_origin;``` Shows warm-pool p95=20, p50=15; primary p95=420, p50=200. Merged p95=130, p50=210.
Ravi: That output nails it. Proposed fixes: - keep per-origin tdigest and a per-origin effective_weight in rollup metadata - compute global percentiles by weight-aware merge or by computing percentiles from combined weighted histogram instead of blind tdigest merge.
Claire: UI/UX suggestions: - add a small "percentile provenance" toggle on the latency chart (options: merged, per-origin overlay, weighted-merge). - add a compact histogram sparkline per-origin in the tooltip. - surface a yellow flag if p95 < p50 or if ordering flips beyond 50ms.
Jordan: Alerting: create an automated check that runs at the end of each aggregation window: if merged_p95 < merged_p50 OR merged_p50 > mean(p50_by_origin)+N*stddev then emit an alert with likely root cause scores (sampling_bias=0.8, bucket_artifact=0.2) and links to per-origin panels.
Maya: Short-term mitigation: console can fall back to showing "per-origin percentiles" as the canonical values for endpoints that have wide origin variance until the aggregator is updated. That avoids misleading merged pcts.
Ravi: I'll prepare the aggregator PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/4377 which will carry `origin_weights` in rollups and add weight-aware tdigest merge. Also adding docs for when tdigests are unsafe (high origin-variance).
Claire: I'll add the UX PR for console: github.com/redwood/console/pull/1203 with toggle + tooltip + yellow-flag treatment.
MetricsBot: Opened incident INC-2026-031: "percentile-ordering-oddity-us-east-embeddings". Tasks assigned: telemetry weight schema, console toggle, runbook entry. https://redwood/internal/inc/INC-2026-031
Jordan: Can we also schedule a short sync with eng-runtime to avoid surprise routing rollouts without a telemetry smoke check?
Maya: Yes please. Adding eng-runtime + eng-releases to the incident and adding a pre-rollout checklist item: "verify telemetry sample weights and run unit check that merged percentiles don't invert across a 10m test window."
Ravi: For the runbook I'll include a quick SQL to compare merged vs weighted merge: ```WITH origins AS (SELECT sample_origin, count(*) AS n, approx_tdigest(response_ms) td FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/embeddings' AND ts > now()-30m GROUP BY sample_origin) SELECT sample_origin, n, td, approx_percentile(td,0.95) p95_from_td, approx_percentile(td,0.5) p50_from_td FROM origins;``` and instructions to compute a weighted merge using origin weights.
Claire: Great. We'll roll the console toggle behind a feature flag and ship the flag to prod dashboard in the next deploy. :rocket:
